{"kind":"hv-full-content-r7","artifact":"verdict.md","sequence":9,"total":13,"artifactSha256":"8E36FE96DF037CAB1E56DFE2ACFBE22AB5764773E1B7B5C95C894334E118C9F9","content":"_LOG in the launched dotnet test environment before discovery, never truncates after discovery and tests fresh attribute/provider-only attempts plus a selected managed fake in separate positive-control processes. Rationale: A trait exclusion alone cannot prove discovery is inert. The new interval and fail-loud controls close the former invisibility gap; N24 adds a successful ordinary-discovery case. Required outcome: Keep the audit outside test-body initialization and retain the entire discovery-to-exit interval.

**N17 PASS** (high), docs/plans/PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001.md:81, Seam-level zero allocation and determinism. Round 6: PASS. Evidence: D2 measures zero incremental allocations and zero log calls over warmed repeated step calls for both bindings with audit unset, preserves independent deterministic output and rejects deliberately allocating/logging doubles. Current Step/StepCycles paths show why cold resolver work must stay outside the cycle path. Rationale: Adjacent managed tests or an empty log do not establish this native seam invariant. The explicit mock-first and real-bound contract does. Required outcome: Keep cold initialization distinct from warmed measurements and reuse identical assertions with the real seams.

**N18 PASS** (high), docs/plans/PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001.md:91, Cycle/half-cycle units and feasibility. Round 6: PASS. Evidence: D5 defines W CPU cycles = 2W half-cycle records, rejects odd half-cycle requests and arithmetic overflow, and distinguishes low restored clock from high legacy clock. Prelude, permit count and any overshoot tail are recorded. Rationale: The gate cannot silently halve the requested interval or pass an infeasible prelude-only invocation. Required outcome: Preserve the fixed interval and canonical D1 budget exception plus terminal contract in N23.

**N19 FAIL** (medium), docs/plans/PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001.md:61, Exclusive register-export claim survives. Round 6: FAIL. Evidence: R11:54 now includes DMA and BRK, but R12:61 still says the pinned VICE exports a correct register file only at an instruction boundary; section 7:164 claims every exclusive list was replaced. Both active CPU sources include 6510dtvcore.c. Its FETCH_OPCODE at 1804 precedes BRK dispatch at 1845-1847; BRK calls EXPORT_REGISTERS at 1012 before INC_PC/DO_IRQBRK. c64/c64cpusc.c:124-179 has already advanced opcode-fetch clocks at that point. Rationale: BRK supplies a concrete export after fetch cycles and before the instruction completes. This does not create an externally requestable arbitrary-cycle checkpoint. The public trap design remains valid, but the global exclusive source claim is still inaccurate and contradicts the requested N19 propagation correction. Required outcome: Replace the global exclusivity claim with the narrow checkpoint claim: the public trap seam used here runs at the boundary whose copied pending mask includes IK_TRAP, with complete exported registers. A request inside an instruction can be delayed; acceptance uses the actual write clock. Search every plan copy, including R11/R12 and section 7, without claiming universal export exclusivity.

**N20 PASS** (high), docs/plans/PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001.md:81, Shared Test/CiTest selector and cumulative projection. Round 6: FAIL. Evidence: Live Build.cs:112 and :140 carry separate copies of the ordinary filter. D2 now explicitly creates one shared selector for both with existing exclusions plus Category!=ShimLegacy&Category!=VsfSlice1Real. The cumulative target selects Category=VsfSlice1Real, stable blocked IDs and nonzero exit. Projection controls run at D2 and after D5 registration with retained per-gate IDs. Rationale: The amendment directly addresses both source copies and prevents the prior chain deadlock: ordinary gates retain contract cases, while blocked real cases remain visible only in the nonpassing cumulative denominator. selector-projection.json independently models these requirements; it is not execution of a future target. Required outc"}
